title: When a traversal meets a change

questions.stem: A for-each loop over `new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b", "c"))` calls `list.remove(item)` when `item` is `"b"`. Per this page, what happens?

options.text: No exception is thrown, and "c" is never visited
options.says: The page says removing the second-to-last element throws nothing: hasNext() sees cursor == size and the loop silently ends, skipping "c".
The page says this case throws nothing, because hasNext() already reports the end.

options.text: No exception is thrown, and "c" is visited as usual
options.says: The page says the loop ends early and silently skips the last element.

questions.stem: Per this page, why must a program not count on `ConcurrentModificationException` to detect another thread's writes to an `ArrayList`?

options.text: modCount is not volatile, so another thread's change may go unseen
options.says: The page says the check is best-effort: modCount is not volatile, so its read may not reflect the latest write from another thread.

options.text: modCount is kept per thread, so another thread's change is never counted
options.says: The page says each collection keeps one modCount field, which every structural change increments.

options.text: modCount is checked by the compiler, so a change at run time is not seen
options.says: The page says the iterator compares modCount at run time, on each next() and remove().
